# A closed subgroup of `C × H` generated by descended commutators

This module builds the candidate common refinement for the proof of
`CentralIsogenyCommonSemisimpleRefinement`. Let `π : C ⟶ G` and `q : H ⟶ G` be
homomorphisms of group schemes whose full scheme-theoretic kernels are central. The
candidate is the closed subgroup `D` of the product group `C × H` generated by the image of

    ambientMap π q hπ hq : G × G ⟶ C × H,
    (π x, π y) ↦ (x y x⁻¹ y⁻¹, x' y' x'⁻¹ y'⁻¹)   where π x = q x', π y = q y'.

Both coordinates are the descended commutator morphisms `CommutatorDescent.hom` of the module
`CentralIsogeny/CommutatorDescent`. The module proves three things.

- On `D` the two composites `D → C → G` and `D → H → G` agree.
- If `C` and `H` are perfect, both projections from `D` are dominant.
- Over a field, `D` exists and is smooth, affine and geometrically connected.

It does not prove that the projections are central isogenies, or that `D` is semisimple.
Those steps are separate.

## Base section: arbitrary base scheme `S`

The hypotheses are `hπ : IsCentral (kernelι π)` and `hq : IsCentral (kernelι q)`. The
underlying scheme morphisms of `π` and `q` are quasi-compact, flat and surjective, as instance
arguments; `CommutatorDescent` needs exactly these.

- `ambientMap` is `lift (CommutatorDescent.hom π hπ) (CommutatorDescent.hom q hq)`, a morphism
  of schemes over `S` from `G.X ⊗ G.X` to `(C ⊗ H).X`. Its two projections are recorded as
  `ambientMap_fst` and `ambientMap_snd`.
- `one_ambientMap` shows that the pair `(1, 1)` is sent to `1`. This is checked coordinatewise
  through the published `productPointsEquiv` and `CommutatorDescent.one_hom`. It is the pointing
  hypothesis that `pointedImageGeneration` needs.

The remaining results of this section concern an arbitrary representative
`D : GeneratedImage (ambientMap π q hπ hq)`. Such a `D` is a group scheme `D.group` with a closed
subgroup inclusion `D.inclusion` into `C ⊗ H`, and it represents the closed envelope of the
image (`GroupScheme/ImageGeneration`).

- `factor_fst` / `factor_snd`: the canonical factor `D.factor : G × G ⟶ D.group.X`, followed by
  the first (second) projection of the subgroup, is the descended commutator for `π` (for `q`).
  This follows from `D.factor_comp` and `ambientMap_fst` / `ambientMap_snd`.
- `factor_fst_comp` / `factor_snd_comp`: following with `π` (with `q`) gives the commutator
  morphism `commutatorMap (𝟙 G) (𝟙 G)` of `G`. This is `CommutatorDescent.hom_comp`.
- `powerMap_comp_eq`: for every `n`, the ordered power map `D.powerMap n` followed by
  `(inclusion ≫ fst) ≫ π` equals it followed by `(inclusion ≫ snd) ≫ q`. Both sides are rewritten
  with the published `orderedPowerMap_comp` as ordered powers of the commutator of `G`.
- `fst_comp_eq_snd_comp`: suppose `D.group.X.left` is reduced, `G.X.hom` is separated, and some
  `(D.powerMap n).left` is dominant. Then
  `(D.inclusion ≫ fst C H) ≫ π = (D.inclusion ≫ snd C H) ≫ q`. Two morphisms from a reduced scheme
  to a separated scheme that agree after a dominant morphism are equal; this is Mathlib's
  `ext_of_isDominant_of_isSeparated`, applied to `powerMap_comp_eq`. `Grp.hom_ext` then gives
  equality of group homomorphisms.

### Dominance from perfectness

Here `derivedSubgroup K = ⊤` is the published statement that `K` is perfect (`Derived/Basic`):
the full test-scheme derived subgroup functor is everything.

- `isIso_inclusion_of_perfect`: if `K` is perfect, then the inclusion of any representative `E`
  of the closed envelope of `commutatorMap (𝟙 K) (𝟙 K)` is an isomorphism. By the published
  `derivedSubgroup_eq_closedImageEnvelope`, the range of `E.inclusion` is `⊤`. So the identity
  point of `K` lifts through `E.inclusion`, which makes it a split epimorphism. It is also a
  monomorphism, because `E` represents its range. Hence it is an isomorphism.
- `isDominant_orderedPowerMap_of_perfect`: if moreover `(E.powerMap m).left` is dominant, then so
  is the ordered power `orderedPowerMap (commutatorMap (𝟙 K) (𝟙 K)) m`. It equals
  `E.powerMap m ≫ E.inclusion` (`GeneratedImage.powerMap_comp`), a dominant map followed by an
  isomorphism.
- `isDominant_fst`: let `C` be perfect, and let `E` be a representative of the commutator
  envelope of `C` with a dominant ordered power `m`. Then the underlying morphism of
  `D.inclusion ≫ fst C H` is dominant. The key identity is

      orderedPowerMap comm_C m = finitePowerMap (π × π) m ≫ D.powerMap m ≫ (D.inclusion ≫ fst C H).

  It is proved with the published `orderedPowerMap_comp`, `orderedPowerMap_precomp`,
  `factor_fst` and `CommutatorDescent.fac`. The left side is dominant by the previous lemma. A
  composite can be dominant only if its last factor is (`IsDominant.of_comp`).
- `isDominant_snd` is the same statement for `H`, `q` and the second projection.

## Field section: `S = Spec k`

- `smooth_tensor`: the product of two smooth group schemes over `Spec k` is smooth. Its structure
  morphism is a base change of a smooth morphism followed by a smooth morphism.
- `one_commutatorMap`: the commutator morphism sends `(1, 1)` to `1` (`commutatorMap_lift`).
- `exists_closedSubgroup`: let `C`, `H` and `G` be smooth, affine and connected over a field
  `k`. Let `π` and `q` have central kernels and be quasi-compact, flat and surjective, and let `C`
  and `H` be perfect. Then there are a group scheme `D` over `Spec k` and a homomorphism
  `i : D ⟶ C ⊗ H` such that
  - `i` is a closed subgroup inclusion;
  - `D.X.hom` is smooth, affine and geometrically connected;
  - `(i ≫ fst C H) ≫ π = (i ≫ snd C H) ≫ q`;
  - the underlying scheme morphisms of `i ≫ fst C H` and `i ≫ snd C H` are dominant.

  Proof. The published `smoothConnectedAffineGeometry` makes `G × G`, `C × C`, `H × H` and
  `C × H` affine; the three squares are also of finite type and geometrically integral. The
  published proved `ImageGeneration.pointedImageGeneration` applies in three places. For the
  smooth affine group `C ⊗ H`, the source `G × G`, the point `(1, 1)` and `ambientMap`, it gives a
  representative `D` that is smooth, affine and geometrically connected, with a dominant ordered
  power `n`. For the commutator morphisms of `C` and of `H`, it gives representatives `E` and `F`
  with dominant ordered powers. `D.group.X.left` is reduced because it is smooth over a field
  (`SmoothReducedProof.isReduced_of_smooth_over_field`). `G.X.hom` is separated because it is
  affine. The equation of composites is then `fst_comp_eq_snd_comp`, and the dominance claims are
  `isDominant_fst` with `E` and `isDominant_snd` with `F`.

## Scope and provenance

No result here is an original-literature theorem. The module is internal infrastructure for
the proof of `CentralIsogenyCommonSemisimpleRefinement`. The idea is the classical one: the
commutator morphism of a central extension factors through the quotient. Applying it to `π`
and `q`, the derived group of the fibre product `C ×_G H` maps onto the derived groups of `C`
and `H`. Here this is realized as a closed subgroup of the smooth group `C × H`, which is where
the published generation theorem applies. Perfectness of `C` and `H` is a hypothesis of
`exists_closedSubgroup`, not something proved here; for semisimple groups it is Milne,
*Algebraic Groups* (2017), Corollary 21.50.
